title: F13: RTL pid truncation at VCS>=4 — tptr > 255 wraps the 8-bit pid field (flit loss at 15-cell vc2 cells)
description: NEW BUG found 2026-08-14 (Laura, 15-cell acceptance): b10_vc2 with VCS=4 binary — injected=3228 ejected=578, FAIL. Deterministic, reproducible (twice). RTL pids 1..1043, BookSim 0..5944; 65/135 (src,pid) pairs have multiple itimes = pid REUSE. Root cause: nic.sv:487 unicast pid = {8'h00, tptr+idx} — 11-bit tptr (T_W=11, T_DEPTH=2048) truncated to 8 bits; tptr>=256 wraps and collides. At VCS=2 traces stayed under 256 so never fired; VCS=4 (longer traces) crosses it. Contrast: b10_vc1 (VCS=2) PASSES the two-tier gate (71,832 flits). The diff's (src,cl,pid) keying cannot fix RTL-side non-unique pids. FIX: widen pid to 16 bits (tptr+idx fits) or reserve a full byte for tptr. VCS=4/8 builds are ALSO environment-blocked (see 0344) — this bug was found on the VCS=4 binary that DID build.

title: Environment: build dirs destroyed mid-test — 6 builds lost today (systemic tooling race)
description: 2026-08-14: six builds destroyed by environment/tooling races — 2x 2-die VCS=8 elab deaths, 1x single-die VCS=8, 1x 2-die VCS=4 elab, 1x VCS=4 g++ compile (verilated.mk:275), and the vbuild_table route-table binary vanished between 10:19 (built) and 10:38 (gone, dir wiped+rewritten by a parallel rebuild). Pattern: long-lived verilator processes or their Mdirs get killed/deleted mid-flight without error. F14's '0 flits' verdicts (10:22-31) are suspect because the binary was mid-rebuild. RULES: (a) verify binary exists + mtime fresh BEFORE every test, (b) capture stdout to a file for every run, (c) one build owner at a time (GATE-R1-COORD board), (d) when a build dies, check for a parallel rebuild before trusting any result.

title: RTL 2-die: SINGLE-packet cross-die deadlock at VCS=2 (table-routing build)
description: ROOT CAUSE FOUND (Steve, 2026-08-14, table-walk forensics): RTL-vs-anynet topology divergence at the bridge nodes. noc_2die.sv merges the bridge into A(7,3)'s EAST and B(0,3)'s WEST ports (mesh links removed); bridged_2die.anynet still contains those mesh links (line 169 router 59 router 60; line 184 router 66 router 67). BookSim-exact Dijkstra tables route die-B west-of-bridge traffic through the phantom links -> at B(0,3) table port W = the bridge -> packet loops across the bridge forever (reproduced: 0->...->59->67->LOOP->59). onecell dst B(0,0) is west of the bridge. FIX (Dave's lane): remove the 2 anynet lines, regenerate tables (staged at /var/tmp/r1work/fixed_tables, 18/128 differ), rebuild, re-run onecell + F14. BookSim must use the fixed anynet for parity. This also re-frames 0344: the deadlock was this divergence, not VC capacity (d7fce0b's table approach was right; the tables inherited the phantom links).

title: Workflow: background builds die with session (nohup, tmux, setsid all killed)
description: Confirmed + data point (Steve, 2026-08-14 12:26): the background-killer fired on a TMUX-launched sim (f14_fixed_test via 'tmux new-session -d'), SIGTERM (EXIT=15) ~6 min into a 7-min run — no OOM (mem was fine), no timeout (600s not reached), no crash (no fatal in log). tmux does NOT reliably protect background sims on this box. Foreground-only rule stands. Workaround in use: relaunch + poll aggressively (30-60s), accept occasional relaunch. Risk applies equally to the concurrent bthru sim + vc1 regen loop.

title: gen_route_tables.py: anynet port numbering is file-order not geometric — bridge must be special-cased
description: BookSim anynet assigns ports by appearance order in the .anynet file (router 59's bridge link = outport 4), but RTL ports are geometric {E,W,N,S,L}. First version of gen_route_tables.py derived port geometrically -> router 59 gave die-B dsts port S instead of E, and die-B 67 gave W for die-A (correct by luck) but the reverse was wrong. Fixed in gen_route_tables.py: bridge directions forced E (die A) / W (die B) via bridge[] map. Lesson: any routing-table generator must map BookSim outports -> RTL geometry, not assume they align.

title: RTL 2-die deadlock: routing divergence from BookSim min_anynet is the ROOT CAUSE (supersedes VC-count theory)
description: BookSim min_anynet = Dijkstra + std::map tie-break (ascending neighbor id, strict <). RTL DOR diverges on 4320/16256 pairs INCLUDING local die-A traffic (8->1: BS N, RTL E). BookSim at num_vcs=1 delivers everything (507-596 cyc) -> 1-VC bridge is NOT structurally deadlock-prone (Laura's seed 0344 'structural' claim revised). Fix: route2d -> table lookup route_<MY_ID>.hex (gen_route_tables.py, Dijkstra-exact). Committed d7fce0b. Residual: single-packet stall (seed ab55) under investigation.
